text:
arin: throwing this out for quick feedback we're debating a thin ribbon vs a micro-spotlight for first-run sample projects. goal: high discovery, low friction.

zoe: ribbon = simple and safe. micro-spotlight drives clicks in tests but feels intrusive to some.

matt: engineering: ribbon is ~3 days, spotlight ~5 because of focus trap and layering. ribbon also plays nicer with responsive grid.

claire: from research, users who clicked a sample project within first session completed onboarding faster. micro-spotlight increased clicks but added confusion for keyboard users.

a11y-bot: a11y checklist: 1) visible focus for CTAs, 2) aria-live polite announcement on show, 3) dismiss must have aria-label (e.g., "Dismiss onboarding ribbon"), 4) persistent dismiss via localStorage, 5) respects prefers-reduced-motion.

arin: proposal: default to ribbon for everyone, behind a flag enable spotlight for an A/B at 10% of new orgs. both must include keyboard order and SR copy.

zoe: copy vote: "Try sample project" for primary, secondary "See sample projects", dismiss visible text "Not now" with aria-label as suggested.

matt: i'll add flags: onboarding_ui= ribbon|spotlight, onboarding_experiment_pct=10, and a kill switch. will instrument events: onboarding.impression, onboarding.cta_click (project_slug), onboarding.dismiss.

claire: QA notes: test high-zoom (200%), low-contrast, keyboard nav, screen reader announcement when banner appears, and that dismiss persists for new sessions.

arin: thanks — i'll add this to ticket ONB-2720 with figma links and microcopy. quick follow-up review after eng PR. :sparkles:
